subject: FSE2
body: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
options: The shop was closed we; went home instead.
The shop was; closed, we went home instead.
The shop; was closed we went home instead.
The shop was closed; we went home instead.
explanation: A semicolon can join two closely related complete sentences.

subject: FSE2
body: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
options: Bring three things a pen: a calculator and photo ID.
Bring three things: a pen, a calculator and photo ID.
Bring: three things a pen, a calculator and photo ID.
Bring three: things, a pen a calculator and photo ID.
explanation: A colon can introduce a list.

subject: FSE2
body: Which correctly shows results belonging to several students?
explanation: For a plural ending in s, add the apostrophe after the s.

subject: FSE2
body: Which sentence uses 'its' correctly?
options: The company changed it is logo last year.
The company changed it's logo last year.
The company changed its logo last year.
The company changed its' logo last year.
explanation: 'It's' means 'it is' or 'it has'.

subject: FSE2
body: Which sentence uses commas correctly around extra information?
options: My manager, who started in May, is very supportive.
My, manager who started in May is very supportive.
My manager who started in May, is, very supportive.
My manager who started, in May is very supportive.
explanation: Commas mark off extra (non-essential) information.

subject: FSE2
body: Which sentence avoids a comma splice?
options: It was, raining we cancelled the match.
It was raining, we cancelled the match.
It was raining we cancelled, the match.
It was raining, so we cancelled the match.
explanation: Two full sentences can't be joined by a comma alone.

subject: FSE2
body: Which spelling is correct for the word meaning 'a place to stay'?
explanation: Double c and double m.

subject: FSE2
body: Which spelling is correct for the word meaning 'certainly'?
explanation: It contains the word 'finite'.

subject: FSE2
body: Which spelling is correct for the word meaning 'to make someone feel awkward'?
explanation: Double r and double s.

subject: FSE2
body: Which spelling is correct for the word meaning 'the group that runs a country'?
explanation: Don't forget the n.

subject: FSE2
body: Choose the correct word: 'The new policy will ___ all staff.'
explanation: 'Affect' is usually a verb; 'effect' is usually a noun.

subject: FSE2
body: Choose the correct word: 'Please send me the ___ by Friday.'
explanation: Stationery means paper and pens; stationary means not moving.

subject: FSE2
body: Choose the correct word: 'Her ___ was helpful in the meeting.'
explanation: 'Advice' is the noun; 'advise' is the verb.

subject: FSE2
body: Choose the correct verb: 'Neither of the proposals ___ acceptable.'
explanation: 'Neither' takes a singular verb.

subject: FSE2
body: Choose the correct verb: 'Each of the managers ___ a parking space.'
explanation: 'Each' is singular, so it takes 'has'.

subject: FSE2
body: Which sentence keeps the tense consistent?
options: She opened the door and sees the parcel.
She opens the door and saw the parcel.
She opening the door and saw the parcel.
She opened the door and saw the parcel.
explanation: Don't switch tense without a reason.

subject: FSE2
body: Which sentence is written in the passive voice?
options: The report was written by the manager.
The manager is writing the report.
The manager will write the report.
explanation: In the passive, the object of the action comes first.

subject: FSE2
body: Choose the correct word: 'There were ___ people at the event than last year.'
explanation: Use 'fewer' for things you can count.

subject: FSE2
body: A text that tries to make you buy a product is mainly
explanation: Look for persuasive techniques such as emotive language.

subject: FSE2
body: Which is an example of a persuasive technique?
options: a rhetorical question such as 'Why wait any longer?'
explanation: Others include statistics, repetition and the rule of three.

subject: FSE2
body: Biased writing
options: presents only one side and may leave out important facts
explanation: Compare sources to judge reliability.

subject: FSE2
body: A fact is
options: something that can be proved true
explanation: Opinions express what someone thinks.

subject: FSE2
body: Which sentence is an opinion?
options: The park is open from 8 am.
The new park opened in June.
The new park is the best place in town.
explanation: 'Best' shows a personal judgement.

subject: FSE2
body: Emotive language is used to
options: explain a process step by step
make the reader feel strongly about something
explanation: For example, 'heartbreaking' or 'shocking'.

subject: FSE2
body: A text says a bus route will use Market Street instead of High Road 'because of roadworks'. Why is the route changing?
options: because the bus company has closed
because of roadworks on High Road
explanation: Identify the reason the text gives.

subject: FSE2
body: Which is the most appropriate opening for a formal letter of complaint?
options: Hi, so basically there was a problem.
I am writing to complain about the service I received on 3 May.
You lot really let me down!
explanation: State your purpose clearly and politely.

subject: FSE2
body: Which connective best shows contrast?
explanation: 'Furthermore' adds; 'therefore' shows a result.

subject: FSE2
body: Which connective best shows a result?
explanation: It links a cause to its effect.

subject: FSE2
body: In a report, the conclusion should
options: introduce new ideas not covered before
summarise the findings and any recommendations
explanation: Keep it brief and clear.

subject: FSE2
body: In a formal discussion, which is the best way to disagree?
options: You don't know what you're talking about.
I see your point, but I think the evidence suggests otherwise.
explanation: Be polite and support your view with evidence.
